reason: Veins and midveins 'level (with the surface)' are neither raised nor sunken: PATO:0002518 flush, 'level or even with another surface'. When a second part is named ('level with apex'), use the relational PATO:0002443 level with and its second term through the 'towards' slot.

label: neuter
definition: A sterile quality inhering in a flower by virtue of its having neither functional stamens nor a functional gynoecium.
reason: A neuter flower lacks working male and female organs. PATO:0000956 sterile is broader, since a flower whose only organs are female-sterile is also sterile. A child of sterile keeps the botanical meaning and stays consistent with unisexual and polygamous.
Hoary means covered with fine greyish-white hairs, which is the definition of FLOPO canescent; 'hoary to cinereous' fits as well.
'Without a claw' on petals and banner petals negates FLOPO clawed. The previous review rejected 'claw' as a generic part, so the claw cannot be treated as an absent part.
Tetragonous means four-angled, which is the same reading as rule C311 (tetragonal → PATO:0001988 quadrangular).

label: chasmogamous
definition: An open quality inhering in a flower by virtue of its opening at anthesis, so that its anthers and stigmas are exposed and it can be cross-pollinated.
reason: This is the positive counterpart of FLOPO:0991176 cleistogamous (a child of closed), and floras contrast the two kinds of flower on one plant. 'Not cleistogamous' would lose the positive statement that the flower opens.

label: monocarpic
definition: A multi-cellular organismal disposition inhering in a plant by virtue of its flowering and fruiting only once and then dying.
reason: This is not a life span: monocarpic perennials exist, so it is independent of PATO annual and perennial life span. PATO has no reproductive-pattern term for it. Bearer: whole plant.
Russet is a reddish-brown colour. PATO:0070059 rusty is a different thing (a texture, covered by iron oxide) and must not be used.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: qualitative_value_relation between lanceolate PATO_0001877 and linear PATO_0001199)
reason: A compound of two shape values, handled like 'linear-lanceolate' by the existing continuum representation.

label: hypogynous
definition: A positional quality inhering in a floral organ or flower by virtue of the perianth and stamens being inserted on the receptacle below the ovary and free from it.
reason: Floras state it of stamens, calyx and flowers, not of the ovary, so FLOPO:0991131 superior (sensu botany), a quality of the ovary, cannot carry it without changing the bearer. Natural sibling for later perigynous and epigynous.

label: polygonal
definition: A 2-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's outline or cross-section having several, usually five or more, straight sides meeting at angles.
reason: Common for leaf cells (bryophytes), seeds and gemmae. PATO has triangular, quadrangular and hexagonal but no general many-sided shape; PATO:0001977 angular ('at least one salient angle') is too broad.
Most uses are French bark or wood 'tendre' and soft plants or fruits, which give little resistance to pressure. On whole plants it can also mean frost-sensitive; those rows should be checked.
Declinate stamens, styles and staminal columns are bent or curved downward towards the lower side of the flower, which is FLOPO descending (directed obliquely downward).
Minutely bumpy lemmas, paleas and seeds have many very small rounded projections, which is PATO:0002427 knobbled (the same target as rule C331 nodose).

label: palmatisect
definition: A dissected quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being cut to or almost to the base into segments radiating from a common point.
reason: The palmate sibling of FLOPO:0991155 pinnatisect, beside FLOPO:0991158 palmately lobed. Forms like '3-5-palmatisect' also carry a count (docs/odp/03-count-of-parts.md).

label: bistratose
definition: A stratified quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being two cell layers thick.
reason: A standard bryophyte character of leaf laminae and margins. PATO stratified does not give the number of layers, and a cell layer is not a PO class that a count could use.
Beardless petals, styles and staminodes negate FLOPO bearded.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md slot 1 (part of the bearer): vascular bundle (PO_0005020) + purple (PATO_0000951)
reason: The colour belongs to the veins of the petal, lip or sepal, not to the organ as a whole, so it is a value stated of a part of the bearer. The same split covers other '<colour>-veined' words.
Knotty rhizomes, bases and branches bear knob-like swellings. Same reading as rule C331 (nodose → knobbled).
A spelling variant of imbricate (overlapping like tiles).
Clambering means climbing by leaning on other vegetation; same reading as rule C355 (scrambling → climbing), restricted to whole plant, stem and branch.
Deltoid is an exact synonym of PATO triangular, so obdeltoid is triangular with the broad end away from the attachment point, which is FLOPO obtriangular.
'Without ribs' on fruits, achenes and stems negates FLOPO ribbed. 'Rib' was rejected as a generic part, so this is not a part absence.
Thin-textured leaves, petals and sepals are thin. FLOPO membranous would add translucency, which the word does not say.
'Leaves elaminate proximally, laminate distally' and 'corolla distally laminate' mean a blade is present. 'Pith laminate' (chambered pith) is a different sense and should not take this rule.

The firm content is that the stem or plant is branched; 'diffusely' (loosely spreading in all directions) is not the wide angle of FLOPO divaricate. It also does not match FLOPO straggly, whose definition requires long irregular branches.

label: anatropous
definition: An inverted quality inhering in an ovule by virtue of its being turned back on its funicle, so that the micropyle lies beside the funicle's point of attachment and the funicle is fused along the side of the ovule as a raphe.
reason: A basic ovule character with no PATO term; its siblings orthotropous and campylotropous would follow. Restrict the bearer to plant ovule (PO:0020003); 'pinnules anatropous' is a fern usage or a misreading.
Coalescent stamens, sepals, carpels and keels are like parts grown together, which is FLOPO connate. 'Veinlets coalescent' is closer to anastomosing and should be checked.

label: necked
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being abruptly narrowed at one end, usually the apex, into a short, more or less cylindrical neck-like part.
reason: Capsules, nutlets, spathes and bulb tunics 'with a neck'. FLOPO beaked (pointed prolongation) and flask-shaped (whole outline) do not fit, and 'neck' was rejected as a generic part. A sibling of FLOPO clawed, which is a narrowing at the base.

label: umbilicate
definition: A concave 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a small central depression, like a navel, at its apex or base.
reason: A standard term for fruits, calyces, capitula and seeds that PATO lacks. PATO:0001857 concave would lose the small, central, navel-like depression.
